# Robot Vacuums: Best Under $300 – November 2026

Last updated November 11, 2026

## We’ve Independently Tested 205+ Robot Vacuums

 Welcome to Vacuum Wars’ pick for the best robot vacuum under $300! Because Vacuum Wars remains independent and buys every model we test, our picks are based on hard data (not advertising claims). We’ve put over 205 robot vacuums through the same trials, and we know many low-cost models cut corners. But our rigorous testing has uncovered the budget-friendly units that still offer solid cleaning, decent navigation, and useful features. In short, you don’t need to break the bank to keep your floors tidy, and our top pick proves it. For more on our testing and scoring, see: Why You Can Trust Vacuum Wars Robot Vacuum Reviews.

Ranking note: Our picks can change as new test results, pricing, availability, and owner satisfaction data are added.

## Best Robot Vacuum Under $300: Dreame D20+

Dreame D20+

$369.99

2.92

$278.99

### Dreame D20+

Vacuum Wars Stars 2.92

The Dreame D20+ is a robot vacuum and mop combo with a self-emptying dock, efficient navigation, and strong vacuuming performance. In Vacuum Wars testing, it removed 93% of embedded debris from carpet and 91% of flattened pet hair, while completing our long-hair tangle test with no hair wrapped around its brushes. It also scored well above average in navigation and battery efficiency, making it a practical choice for larger homes. The D20+ offers multi-level mapping, virtual barriers, carpet boost, adjustable mopping water levels, and app and voice controls. While its mopping system is basic and it lacks dedicated obstacle avoidance, its impressive carpet cleaning, pet hair pickup, and convenient self-emptying dock make it a strong option for households that prioritize vacuuming performance. Self-emptying dock Strong carpet cleaning Pet-hair pickup Tangle resistance Room mapping Carpet boost +2 more

Read the full Vacuum Wars review

$278.99

11/12/2026 09:38 pm GMT

Price matters for this pick: the Dreame D20+ is our Best Robot Vacuum Under $300 selection when its current selling price falls below that limit. Check the live price in the product card before buying. Our recommendation focuses on its vacuuming strengths, rather than expecting premium mopping or obstacle avoidance at this price.

## Why We Picked the Dreame D20+

The Dreame D20+ earned this budget recommendation because its strongest results are in the areas that matter for routine vacuuming: carpet cleaning, pet hair, battery efficiency, and navigation. In our studio test report, it delivered:

- 93% carpet deep-cleaning pickup, compared with a 77.86% test average.
- 91% flattened pet-hair pickup, above the 82.2% average.
- 0% hair tangle in our 7-inch hair test, compared with a 26% average.
- Estimated coverage of about 2,761 square feet per charge, well above the 1,170-square-foot average.
- A 4.11 performance score, above the Vacuum Wars average of 3.54.

The D20+ also comes with a self-emptying station, reducing how frequently you need to empty its onboard dustbin. The trade-off is straightforward: it is better equipped for vacuuming than for heavy-duty mopping, and it lacks dedicated obstacle avoidance.

The Dreame D20+ robot vacuum with its self-emptying station at the Vacuum Wars studio. © Vacuum Wars

## Where the Dreame D20+ Stands Out

### Excellent Carpet Deep Cleaning

Our carpet deep-cleaning test evaluates how much embedded debris a robot removes, rather than judging only what it can sweep from the surface. The Dreame D20+ removed 93% of the embedded material, compared with a 77.86% average. That’s a compelling result for a vacuum in this price category.

Its bench measurements were more mixed: 0.53 kPa suction against a 0.99 kPa average, and 18 CFM airflow against a 16.95 CFM average. The lower suction reading makes the actual carpet-cleaning result especially useful. A single power specification does not fully predict cleaning performance.

The Dreame D20+ undergoing carpet deep-cleaning evaluations at the Vacuum Wars studio, where it removed 93% of embedded debris, compared with the 77.86% average. © Vacuum Wars

### Strong Pet Hair Pickup and Tangle Resistance

In our test using 2.5-inch pet hair flattened into carpet, the D20+ collected 91%, outperforming the 82.2% test average. That makes it a strong contender for households where pet hair accumulates on rugs or carpet.

It also returned 0% hair tangle in our controlled test with 7-inch hair, compared with the 26% average. That does not guarantee a completely maintenance-free brush, but it is a particularly good test result for people concerned about wrapped hair.

The D20+ had strong pet hair pickup performance in our studio evaluations. © Vacuum Wars

### A Self-Emptying Station

The D20+ includes an automatic dust-emptying station. The robot returns to its dock, which transfers debris from the onboard bin so you do not have to empty it after every session. The report also lists an adjustable auto-empty frequency and an onboard dustbin capacity of 500 mL.

This is not a full-service mop dock. The D20+ does not wash or dry mop pads, replenish mop water, or automate mop maintenance. The main convenience is dust collection.

The Dreame D20+ self-emptying station collects debris in a disposable dust bag, reducing the need to manually empty the robot’s onboard dustbin. © Vacuum Wars

### Efficient Navigation

The D20+ performed well in mapping and route efficiency. Its measured navigation speed was 0.75 square meters per minute, compared with an average of 0.711. It took 5 minutes to map our test area, against a 9.78-minute average, and completed the reported vacuum-and-mop run in 48 minutes, compared with 56.36 minutes on average.

The navigation score was 4.77, above the 3.06 average. It can plan an orderly cleaning route, but navigation performance should not be confused with small-object obstacle avoidance; that is a separate weakness below.

The Dreame D20+ navigating a furnished room during our evaluations. It demonstrated above-average navigation efficiency, covering 0.75 square meters per minute compared with the 0.711 average. © Vacuum Wars

### Exceptional Battery Efficiency

Battery performance was another standout. In our battery-efficiency test, the D20+ recorded 3.42 minutes per 1% of battery, compared with a 1.56-minute average. Its test-derived estimated coverage was approximately 2,761 square feet per charge, more than twice the supplied average of 1,170 square feet.

The manufacturer battery-life figure recorded in our report is 285 minutes. That advertised figure is separate from our battery-efficiency test and our estimated coverage. Actual runtime and area cleaned depend on settings, floor conditions, layout, and cleaning mode.

### Useful App and Room Controls

The D20+ offers multi-level maps, room-specific settings, custom cleaning sequence, virtual barriers, no-mop zones, zone cleaning, and recharge-and-resume operation. The feature report also lists carpet boost, 3D mapping, and compatibility with Alexa or Google Assistant.

Those controls are valuable for tailoring a budget robot to different rooms. They do not, however, enable it to identify and steer around every loose object on the floor.

## What You Give Up at This Price

### Basic Mopping and Below-Average Stain Removal

Mopping is a secondary feature on the D20+. It uses a simpler, manually maintained mop setup without automatic pad washing, drying, lifting, or extending. The robot offers adjustable water levels, but no powered scrubbing system is documented in the supplied report.

In our mopping stain test, the D20+ scored 90, below the 107.8 average. Its overall mop score was 1.60, compared with a 2.35 average. The combined mop-and-water result was also below average, at 20.75 versus 24.24.

If your primary concern is dried-on stains and regular automated mopping, this is not the model we would prioritize. It makes more sense as a strong budget vacuum with a basic wiping function.

### No Dedicated Obstacle Avoidance

The D20+ does not have dedicated small-object obstacle avoidance. In the supplied Vacuum Wars obstacle tests, it avoided 0 of 24 objects. That is a meaningful limitation, especially in homes with charging cables, socks, toys, or other small items on the floor.

Its strong LiDAR-style route efficiency does not mean it can recognize clutter. We recommend clearing loose objects before running scheduled cleanings.

The Dreame D20+ navigating our obstacle avoidance test course, where it failed to avoid all 24 test objects. We recommend clearing cords, toys, and other small items before cleaning. © Vacuum Wars

### Manual Mop Maintenance

The self-emptying dock does not wash mop pads or refill the robot’s water. You will need to maintain the mop pad yourself and manage carpet transitions carefully because the D20+ does not lift its mop pad.

### Below-Average Crevice Pickup and Bench Suction

Our test report also recorded a 1.0 crevice pickup score, below the 1.97 average, and a below-average suction bench reading. Homes with deep tile grout or pronounced floorboard gaps may therefore have different priorities from buyers focused on carpet deep cleaning.

## Who Should Choose the Dreame D20+?

The D20+ is best suited to value-focused buyers who prioritize vacuuming, especially carpet and pet hair pickup, and want the convenience of automatic dust emptying. Its strong battery and navigation results also make it attractive for larger or multi-room cleaning areas.

It is a less suitable choice for homes that need reliable avoidance of cords and toys, hands-off mop cleaning, or better dried-on stain removal. Those are substantial compromises, and buying strictly by the overall score could hide them.

## The Bottom Line

The Dreame D20+ is our Best Robot Vacuum Under $300 pick. Its 93% carpet deep-cleaning result, 91% pet-hair pickup, tangle-free controlled hair test, strong route efficiency, and outstanding estimated battery coverage are the reasons it earns that designation.

The trade-off is a basic mop and no meaningful small-object obstacle avoidance. If your priority is an affordable, mostly vacuuming-focused robot with a self-emptying dock, the D20+ deserves a close look whenever its current price is under $300. If you expect advanced mopping or hands-off cleaning around clutter, compare models with those features before buying.

The Dreame D20+ at the Vacuum Wars studio. With excellent carpet cleaning, pet hair pickup, and battery efficiency, it earned our Best Robot Vacuum Under $300 recommendation. © Vacuum Wars

## Compare the Dreame D20+ With Other Robot Vacuums

Use our robot vacuum comparison tool to compare current models and features. For more options beyond this price bracket, see the Vacuum Wars best robot vacuums list.

Best Robot Vacuums – Vacuum Wars’ always up-to-date rankings of the best robot vacuums. Whether you call it a robot vacuum, a robotic hoover, or an automatic vacuum cleaner, our top picks will help you find the perfect cleaning companion for your home!

## Why You Can Trust Vacuum Wars Robot Vacuum Reviews

Vacuum Wars is 100% independent and reader-funded. We pay full retail price for every robot vacuum we test and take no money from manufacturers. Each unit goes through the same rigorous test suite, so our results are impartial and easy to compare. For a detailed breakdown of our robot vacuum testing process, head to our How We Test Robot Vacuums page.

## Finding the Best Robot Vacuum Under $300

If you’re in the market for a robot vacuum but want to avoid the high costs associated with more advanced features, this article is for you. We’ve evaluated a wide array of popular budget robot vacuums over the years, gathering valuable insights to help you make an informed decision. 

### Understanding the Basics

Historically, robot vacuums started with a basic set of features: spinning brush rolls, side brushes, bump sensors, cliff detection, and infrared wall sensors. Their navigation was simple but effective, moving randomly until their battery ran low. Today, while advanced models boast cameras, lasers, and more, the original, budget-friendly designs remain popular due to their simplicity and reduced cost.

### The Market Dynamics

The budget robot vacuum market is unique. Adding features increases cost, so maintaining a balance between functionality and price is key. This balance has made it challenging for new manufacturers to enter the market without inflating prices. Consequently, established brands with the ability to place large manufacturing orders dominate this space, often offering better pricing due to economies of scale.

Budget category robot vacuums at we have evaluated at Vacuum Wars.

### Choosing the Right Robot Vacuum Under $300

When selecting a budget robot vacuum, consider the following:

- Battery Life: Look for a battery life that suits the size of your home. Typically, budget models offer between 90 to 120 minutes of cleaning time.
- Floor Adaptability: Choose a vacuum that can handle the types of floors in your home, whether it’s hard floors or carpets. Some budget models have features that adjust suction power for different floor types.
- Connectivity and Control: While some budget models lack Wi-Fi capability, others offer this feature with app-based controls for added convenience. Consider whether a physical remote or app control best suits your lifestyle.
- Parts Availability: Some models have readily available replacement parts. This ensures the longevity of your vacuum and adds value over time.
- Navigation Efficiency: While they may not have advanced mapping capabilities, many budget models efficiently cover significant areas with their random navigation patterns.
- Performance: Pay attention to suction power and how well the vacuum performs in practical tasks, such as carpet deep cleaning and picking up debris from crevices.

### Choosing your Robot Vacuum

When deciding on the best budget robot vacuum for your needs, balance cost with the features that are most important to you. While you may not get every advanced feature, many budget-friendly options under $300 provide excellent basic cleaning capabilities.

### Conclusion

The best inexpensive robot vacuum is one that meets your specific cleaning needs without unnecessary extras that inflate the cost. By considering the points outlined above, you can find a robot vacuum that provides effective cleaning at a price that doesn’t break the bank.

# Best Budget Robot Vacuums Under $300 (2026)

 Mar 24, 2026 6 min read

 Last updated: Mar 24, 2026

## Table of Contents

Our Budget Picks at a Glance What to Expect Under $300 What You Get What You Give Up 1. eufy L60 — Best Budget Overall Key Specs Performance Who It's For Drawbacks 2. Dreame D10s Plus — Best for Self-Emptying on a Budget Key Specs Performance Who It's For Drawbacks 3. Roborock Q5 Pro+ — Best Carpet Cleaning Under $300 Key Specs Performance Who It's For Drawbacks 4. eufy G40 Hybrid+ — Best Under $200 Key Specs Performance Who It's For Drawbacks Buying Advice for Budget Robot Vacuums Prioritize LiDAR Navigation Self-Emptying Is a Luxury, Not a Necessity Skip Mopping Under $300 Consider Your Floor Types Frequently Asked Questions Are budget robot vacuums worth it? What is the best robot vacuum under $200? Do I need a self-emptying base station? Can a budget robot vacuum handle pet hair? How long do budget robot vacuums last?

You do not need to spend $800 or more to get a robot vacuum that actually works. The budget segment has improved dramatically — several models under $300 now offer LiDAR navigation, decent suction, and reliable app control. We tested eight budget robot vacuums over the past six months to find the ones worth buying.

> 30-Second Summary
> 
> - Best overall under $300: eufy L60 — $229, LiDAR navigation, 5,000Pa suction
> - Best with self-emptying: Dreame D10s Plus — $199 with dock
> - Best for carpet: Roborock Q5 Pro+ — $279, 82% carpet extraction
> - Best under $200: eufy G40 Hybrid+ — $199, basic but reliable

## Our Budget Picks at a Glance

| Rank | Model | Price | Navigation | Suction | Rating |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | eufy L60 | $229 (MSRP $399) | LiDAR | 5,000Pa | 8.3/10 |
| 2 | Dreame D10s Plus | $199 (MSRP $439) | LiDAR | 4,000Pa | 8.0/10 |
| 3 | Roborock Q5 Pro+ | $279 (MSRP $429) | LiDAR | 5,500Pa | 8.1/10 |
| 4 | eufy G40 Hybrid+ | $199 | Gyroscope | 2,500Pa | 7.4/10 |

## What to Expect Under $300

Before diving into individual picks, set realistic expectations.

### What You Get

- LiDAR navigation at $250 and above — accurate room mapping, efficient paths, zone control via app
- Suction between 2,500Pa and 5,500Pa — handles hard floors well and manages light-to-medium carpet debris
- App control with scheduling, room selection, and basic customization
- 120 to 150 minute battery life — enough for apartments and smaller homes

### What You Give Up

- Self-emptying base stations are rare under $300. Most budget robots have manual dustbins.
- Mopping is either absent or basic (gravity-fed water tank with passive pad). Do not expect hot water washing or rotating pads.
- Obstacle avoidance is bumper-based only — no AI cameras at this price.
- Carpet deep cleaning is noticeably weaker: 70-80% embedded debris vs 88-93% for premium models.

The technology gap is shrinking fast, though. As Vacuum Wars noted: "Budget robot vacuums in 2026 aren't 'good for the price' — they're genuinely good. The technology that cost $1,000 in 2023 now costs $200."

## 1. eufy L60 — Best Budget Overall

Price: $279.99 (down from $399) | Rating: 8.3 / 10

The eufy L60 is the our top-rated robot vacuums you can buy under $300, and it is not particularly close. LiDAR navigation, 5,000Pa suction, and surprisingly strong hard floor cleaning at a price that makes the decision easy.

### Key Specs

| Spec | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Suction | 5,000Pa |
| Navigation | LiDAR |
| Battery | 120 minutes |
| Dustbin | 600ml (manual empty) |
| Mopping | None |
| Noise | 60 dB (balanced) |

### Performance

The L60 scored 95.2% on hard floors — remarkable for a $229 robot. The eufy X10 Pro Omni ($449) scored 99.1%. The gap exists but is smaller than the price difference suggests.

Carpet is where the price shows: 78% embedded debris on medium-pile, compared to 93% for the X10 Pro. For homes with mostly hard floors and area rugs, this is a perfectly acceptable trade-off.

One Reddit owner with long-haired border collies reported "still loving it after 7 months of use" — and noted the brush design "cuts hair away from the roller." Another user summed up the value: for hard floor homes, it punches well above its weight.

The flip side: some owners reported roller brush errors and drive wheel failures after 2-3 months. These seem to be batch-specific issues rather than a design flaw, but worth knowing before buying.

### Who It's For

First-time robot vacuum buyers, apartment dwellers, and anyone who wants reliable daily vacuuming without a premium investment. If your home is primarily hard floors, this is a no-brainer.

### Drawbacks

No self-emptying base — empty the dustbin every 1-3 days. No mopping. Bumper-only obstacle avoidance. Carpet cleaning is adequate but not impressive.

## 2. Dreame D10s Plus — Best for Self-Emptying on a Budget

Price: — (down from $439) | Rating: 8.0 / 10

The Dreame D10s Plus is one of the rare budget robots that includes a self-emptying base station. If emptying a dustbin every few days is a dealbreaker, this is your pick.

### Key Specs

| Spec | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Suction | 4,000Pa |
| Navigation | LiDAR |
| Battery | 150 minutes |
| Dustbin | 400ml (robot) / 2.5L (base) |
| Mopping | Basic (gravity-fed) |
| Noise | 63 dB (balanced) |

### Performance

Hard floor cleaning scored 93.1% — solid. Carpet came in at 74%, below the eufy L60. The 4,000Pa suction handles daily maintenance but lacks power for deeply embedded debris.

The self-emptying base works well: empties in about 10 seconds, dust bag lasts ~45 days. Replacement bags are $19.99 for a 4-pack. The mopping function is basic — a gravity-fed water tank dampens a cloth pad. Think light damp wipe, not real mopping.

### Who It's For

Buyers who prioritize convenience. The hands-off dust disposal alone can justify choosing this over the eufy L60 for busy households.

### Drawbacks

Weaker suction than the eufy L60. Rudimentary mopping. Base station adds footprint. Weakest carpet cleaning of our picks.

## 3. Roborock Q5 Pro+ — Best Carpet Cleaning Under $300

Price: — (down from $429) | Rating: 8.1 / 10

The Roborock Q5 Pro+ sits right under our $300 ceiling but delivers the strongest carpet cleaning in the budget segment along with a self-emptying base.

### Key Specs

| Spec | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Suction | 5,500Pa |
| Navigation | LiDAR |
| Battery | 140 minutes |
| Dustbin | 470ml (robot) / 2.5L (base) |
| Mopping | None |
| Noise | 62 dB (balanced) |

### Performance

The Q5 Pro+ benefits from Roborock's brush design expertise: 94.8% on hard floors and 82% on carpet — the best carpet score in this price range. The 5,500Pa suction provides noticeably more extraction than the Dreame's 4,000Pa.

Navigation uses the same LiDAR system as Roborock's premium models. Mapping is fast, room detection is accurate, and the Roborock app provides the same 3D map visualization and room labeling found on the $899 S8 MaxV Ultra. That app advantage alone makes it worth considering.

Self-emptying base is compact and effective — dust bags lasted ~50 days in our testing.

### Who It's For

Buyers with a mix of hard floors and carpet wanting the best cleaning at this price. Also great for existing Roborock app users who want a second robot for another floor.

### Drawbacks

At $279, it is the most expensive option here. No mopping. Bumper-only obstacle avoidance.

## 4. eufy G40 Hybrid+ — Best Under $200

Price: — | Rating: 7.4 / 10

If your budget is closer to $200, the eufy G40 Hybrid+ is the best option. It sacrifices LiDAR for gyroscope navigation but adds basic mopping.

### Key Specs

| Spec | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Suction | 2,500Pa |
| Navigation | Gyroscope |
| Battery | 100 minutes |
| Dustbin | 450ml (manual empty) |
| Mopping | Basic (gravity-fed) |
| Noise | 56 dB (balanced) |

### Performance

Without LiDAR, the G40 Hybrid+ cleans in a semi-random pattern — less efficient but still covers everything given enough time. Hard floor: 89.4%. Carpet: 68%. At 2,500Pa, it handles fine dust well but larger debris and carpet are where the lower power shows.

The quietest robot on this list at 56 dB — you can run it while on a call.

### Who It's For

Budget-first buyers who want hard floor maintenance between manual cleaning sessions. Good starter robot and easy recommendation under $200.

### Drawbacks

Gyroscope navigation is less efficient — no room mapping or zone control. Weaker suction and cleaning across the board. 100-minute battery limits it to apartments.

### Prioritize LiDAR Navigation

The single biggest upgrade is gyroscope → LiDAR. LiDAR robots clean faster, cover more area, miss fewer spots, and support room mapping and zone control. If your budget allows $229+, get a LiDAR model.

### Self-Emptying Is a Luxury, Not a Necessity

Self-emptying adds tremendous convenience, but emptying a dustbin manually takes 30 seconds. If choosing between better cleaning (eufy L60) and self-emptying with weaker suction (Dreame D10s Plus), prioritize cleaning performance.

### Skip Mopping Under $300

No budget robot delivers meaningful mopping. The gravity-fed systems do little more than a damp Swiffer. If mopping matters, save for a mid-range model like the Narwal Freo X Ultra or premium eufy X10 Pro Omni.

### Consider Your Floor Types

Mostly hard floors? Even a $199 robot delivers solid daily maintenance. Significant carpet? Stretch to the eufy L60 or Roborock Q5 Pro+ for noticeably better extraction.

For mid-range and premium options, see our best robot vacuums of 2026 guide. To understand every feature and spec, check our robot vacuum buying guide.

### Are budget robot vacuums worth it?

Yes — the technology gap between budget and premium has shrunk dramatically. A $229 eufy L60 with LiDAR navigation delivers 95.2% hard floor cleaning, compared to 99.1% for a robot costing three times more. For daily hard floor maintenance, a budget robot keeps your home noticeably cleaner with zero effort. The trade-offs are in carpet deep cleaning, mopping, and obstacle avoidance — not in basic vacuuming.

### What is the best robot vacuum under $200?

The eufy G40 Hybrid+ at $199 if you just need basic vacuuming. The Dreame D10s Plus at $199 if you want self-emptying (it is at the $200 boundary and a much better robot thanks to LiDAR navigation). If you can stretch to $229, the eufy L60 is significantly better than both.

### Do I need a self-emptying base station?

It is convenient but not essential. Manually emptying a dustbin takes 30 seconds every 1-3 days. The self-emptying dock is most valuable if you travel often, have pets (more frequent emptying), or simply hate routine maintenance. Between the Dreame D10s Plus ($199 with dock) and Roborock Q5 Pro+ ($279 with dock), the Roborock is the better buy for its superior cleaning performance.

### Can a budget robot vacuum handle pet hair?

On hard floors, yes — any LiDAR model on this list picks up surface pet hair effectively. On carpet, results vary: the Roborock Q5 Pro+ at 82% is adequate for light shedding, but if you have multiple pets or long-haired breeds, you will want a dedicated pet hair model like the Roborock S8 MaxV Ultra with anti-tangle rubber rollers.

### How long do budget robot vacuums last?

With proper maintenance (cleaning brushes weekly, emptying dustbin regularly), expect 2-3 years of reliable service from a quality budget robot. LiDAR sensors and motors are generally durable. The most common failure points are brushes (replaceable, ~$15) and batteries (1-2 year lifespan, ~$30-$50 for replacement). Some eufy L60 owners reported drive wheel issues after 2-3 months, but this appears to be batch-specific rather than a widespread design flaw.

Last updated: April 2026. Prices reflect current street prices and may vary by retailer.

Four of our August picks (eufy Clean L60, Shark ION RV765, Yeedi Vac 2 Pro, eufy RoboVac 11S Max) are discontinued or out of stock new, the Roomba 694 is no longer sold on iRobot’s store, and the Lefant M210 Pro has no US store listing, so this guide has been rebuilt.

For pet hair, the Shark Navigator RV2110 ($149.99 at Target) adds a self-cleaning brushroll to spot LiDAR mapping. The cheapest LiDAR robot from a major brand is the Roborock Q7 L5 ($139.99 in white on Roborock’s US store), but Vacuum Wars measured just 12.25% on its flattened pet-hair test, so buy it only for a pet-free home. Two hundred dollars used to buy a robot that bounced off your walls at random. In November 2026 every robot in this guide maps with LiDAR, and the cheapest one costs $139.99. The catch is churn: budget models come and go fast, and most of the picks we listed in August have since been discontinued or dropped from their brand’s store. Below are five robots you can buy new today, with the price and store we checked on November 6, 2026. If your budget can stretch, our best robot vacuum under $300 guide covers where self-emptying docks come into reach.

- 12.25% vs 81%: Vacuum Wars measured the Q7 L5’s flattened pet-hair pickup against its category average, the worst result it has recorded. Cheap LiDAR does not guarantee good pickup.
- Up to 60 days between bin empties on the dockless Roomba 205 DustCompactor, per iRobot, because it compresses debris inside the robot.

## Measured results, where they exist

Independent lab data is thin at this price. Vacuum Wars has published full measurements for only one of these five robots, the Roborock Q7 L5, in its October 2026 Q7 L5 vs Q7 M5 review.

| Hair tangle (7 in, lower is better) | 56% | 21% |
| Sealed suction | 1.95 kPa | 0.97 kPa |

| Mop water used | 3.35 g | 1.04 g |

For the other four, the specs and owner ratings below come from the brand and Target listings. Target showed the Shark Navigator RV2110 at 3.97 of 5 stars from 129 ratings, the Roomba 205 DustCompactor at 3.78 from 204, and the bObsweep Dustin at 4.2 from 47 on November 6, 2026.

## 1. iRobot Roomba 105 Combo Robot: Best Robot Vacuum Under $200 Overall

### iRobot Roomba 105 Combo Robot

Best overall under $200 · $169.99 on irobot.com (list $319.99)

- ClearView LiDAR maps the home, cleans in rows and works in the dark, per iRobot.
- Vacuums, or vacuums and mops in one run; Carpet Detect keeps the pad off rugs.
- Roomba Home app with room selection and keep-out zones; iRobot says mapping takes about 10 minutes.

The 105 Combo Robot is the most complete package under $200. iRobot cut it from $319.99 to $169.99 on its own store, and at that price you get LiDAR mapping, a 4-stage cleaning system with a multi-surface bristle brush and an edge-sweeping brush, and a mop that iRobot says stays off rugs automatically. It docks on a charging base only; iRobot sells the same robot with an AutoEmpty dock for $269.99. Our iRobot Roomba Combo guide compares it with the rest of iRobot’s 2026 combo lineup. If you already own iRobot’s older entry model, our Roomba Vac Essential review covers how it compares.

## 2. Shark Navigator RV2110: Best for Pet Hair Under $200

### Shark Navigator RV2110

Best for pet hair · $149.99 at Target (list $299.99)

- Self-cleaning brushroll designed against hair wrap.
- Spot LiDAR mapping with SmartPath row-by-row cleaning, plus object detection.
- 0.52 qt bin, recharge and resume, and voice control.

Hair wrapped around the brushroll is the usual budget-robot failure in pet homes, and Shark’s self-cleaning brushroll is built to prevent it. The RV2110 also maps with spot LiDAR and cleans row by row, and Shark says it “detects and avoids objects in its path.” Shark sells the same robot with a self-empty base as the RV2120AE for $229.99 on SharkNinja’s store. Compare it with the rest of the brand in our best Shark robot vacuum guide, and see our best robot vacuum for pet hair for stronger pet picks above $200.

## 3. Roborock Q7 L5: Cheapest LiDAR Robot (Pet-Free Homes Only)

### Roborock Q7 L5

Cheapest LiDAR pick · $139.99 white / $199.99 black on Roborock US

- PreciSense LiDAR, 8,000 Pa rated suction, up to 3 floor maps.
- Vacuum Wars: 80% deep-carpet cleaning and 1,465 sq ft per charge, both above average.
- Only 12.25% flattened pet-hair pickup, 56% long-hair tangling and over-wet mopping.

The Q7 L5 is the cheapest way into LiDAR mapping from a major brand, and in Vacuum Wars’ measurements its motor is strong: 1.95 kPa of sealed suction, about twice the category average. But its brush is the weak link. It picked up only 12.25% of flattened pet hair, the worst result Vacuum Wars has recorded, and 56% of long hair wrapped around the brush. Buy the white model at $139.99 for hard floors in a home without pets; the black one at $199.99 is poor value. Our full Roborock Q7 L5 review compares it with its near-twin, the Q7 M5+.

## 4. iRobot Roomba 205 DustCompactor: Best Without a Dock

### iRobot Roomba 205 DustCompactor

Best without a dock · $199.99 at Target (list $449.99)

- Compresses debris inside the robot's 380 mL bin; iRobot says up to 60 days between empties.
- ClearView LiDAR built into the body, with room scheduling and keep-out zones.
- 4 suction levels; works with Alexa and Siri, per the Target listing.

The 205 DustCompactor solves the same problem as a self-emptying dock without the dock. It crushes debris inside the robot, and iRobot claims up to 60 days of cleaning before you empty it, with no bags and no tall base taking up floor space. It is vacuum-only and sits right at the $200 line at Target’s $199.99 sale price. If you would rather have a mop, the 105 Combo Robot above costs $30 less.

## 5. bObsweep Dustin Self-Empty: The Only Self-Emptying Pick

### bObsweep Dustin Self-Empty

Only self-emptying pick · $189.99 on Target.com, sold by bObsweep (list $625)

- Self-empty dock with a 1-gallon (4.6 L) bag.
- LiDAR mapping; 4,100 to 5,000 Pa rated suction; mop pad included.
- Bluetooth or 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi app, Alexa and Google Assistant.

This was the only new self-emptying robot we found at $200 or less on November 6, 2026, at the price shown for this listing. It is a marketplace listing on Target.com, sold and shipped by bObsweep rather than Target, so check the seller’s return terms before you buy. bObsweep says the warranty is 24 months and covers the battery, while the Target listing shows a 1-year limited warranty. No independent lab has published measurements for it.

## How to choose a robot vacuum under $200

- If you want one robot that vacuums and mops: the Roomba 105 Combo Robot at $169.99.
- If you have a dog or cat: the Shark Navigator RV2110 for its self-cleaning brushroll. Avoid the Roborock Q7 L5.
- If you want the lowest price with mapping and have no pets: the white Roborock Q7 L5 at $139.99.
- If you hate emptying the bin: the Roomba 205 DustCompactor (up to 60 days, no dock) or the bObsweep Dustin (1-gallon self-empty dock).
- If you can spend $30 to $70 more: a self-emptying LiDAR robot from a major brand starts at $229.99 (Shark RV2120AE) to $249.99 (Roborock Q7 M5+, white).

None of these robots has camera-based obstacle avoidance, so pick up cables, socks and pet messes before a run. Ready to spend a little more? ## Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best robot vacuum under $200 in 2026?

For most homes, the iRobot Roomba 105 Combo Robot ($169.99 on irobot.com on November 6, 2026, list $319.99). It maps with ClearView LiDAR, vacuums and mops, and avoids mopping rugs. For pet hair, the Shark Navigator RV2110 ($149.99 at Target) has a self-cleaning brushroll and spot LiDAR mapping. The cheapest LiDAR robot from a major brand is the Roborock Q7 L5 at $139.99 (white) on Roborock's US store, but Vacuum Wars measured only 12.25% on its flattened pet-hair test, so it suits pet-free homes only.

Can you get a robot vacuum with LiDAR mapping under $200?

Yes. Every pick in this guide maps with LiDAR. On November 6, 2026 the cheapest were the Roborock Q7 L5 ($139.99 white, Roborock US), the Shark Navigator RV2110 ($149.99, Target, spot LiDAR), the Roomba 105 Combo Robot ($169.99, iRobot) and the Roomba 205 DustCompactor ($199.99, Target). Mapping lets you pick rooms and draw no-go zones in the app, and the robot cleans in rows instead of bouncing at random.

Is there a self-emptying robot vacuum under $200?

Only one new model turned up on November 6, 2026: the bObsweep Dustin Self-Empty at $189.99 on Target.com (list $625), sold by bObsweep through Target's marketplace, with a 1-gallon (4.6 L) dock. At brand stores the cheapest self-emptying robots cost more: Shark's Navigator RV2120AE $229.99, Roborock's Q7 M5+ $249.99 (white) and iRobot's Roomba 105 Combo with AutoEmpty dock $269.99. The Roomba 205 DustCompactor ($199.99) skips the dock and compacts dust inside the robot instead, for up to 60 days per iRobot.

Can a robot vacuum under $200 also mop?

Yes, lightly. The Roomba 105 Combo Robot, Roborock Q7 L5 and bObsweep Dustin all drag a damp pad. None washes or dries its own mop pad; those docks start around $400. Measured results vary a lot: Vacuum Wars found the Q7 L5 used 3.35 g of water in its mop test, more than three times the 1.04 g average, which left floors overly wet.

Which budget robot vacuums are discontinued?

Several former budget favorites are gone. eufy says the whole L60 series (including the L60 SES) has been discontinued and will not be restocked (eufy blog, July 31, 2026). The Shark ION RV765 no longer appears on SharkNinja's store, the Yeedi Vac 2 Pro is no longer sold on yeedi.com, iRobot's site lists the Roomba 694 as 'available only at select retailers', and the eufy RoboVac 11S Max showed no new stock on eufy's store on November 6, 2026.

Is a robot vacuum under $200 worth it?

For hard floors and low-pile rugs in a tidy home, yes. In 2026 $200 buys LiDAR mapping, app room selection and scheduling. What you give up is a self-emptying dock (with one marketplace exception), a self-washing mop dock and camera-based obstacle avoidance. If you have a shedding pet, check measured pet-hair results before buying: Vacuum Wars measured the $139.99 Roborock Q7 L5 at 12.25%, against an 81% average.
